verdicts.misleading_risk: Several sub-claims were verified, but the proposal bundles a lot. verdicts.misleading_risk: The auditor's cause analysis is half wrong in two places. (1) The link './download_executable.md' in troubleshooting_installed_app.md is correct in the real app repos: NucleiSky/.tools/docs/download_executable.md and CellTracksColab/.tools/docs/download_executable.md each contain per-app install and uninstall text (grep 'uninstall' hits in both). Only the template's own stub is empty, and the page is copied into every app. So the defect is site-only, and the proposal (a) to 'add Uninstall to install.md and repoint' would break the link in the app repos, where install.md does not exist. (2) app.py:685 is not a link to the template's 'no executables yet' stub. It is written into the generated README of the new app repo and points at that repo's own download_executable.md, which is meant to be replaced per app. The proposed form change and test for it would be wrong. Also the uninstall claims are unverified: install.md has no uninstall steps, and uninstall.sh exists only for Linux/macOS; the Windows text rests on the Settings > Apps path in the troubleshooting page.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Two small parts only. (a) Site, scripts/lcsite/guides.py rewrite_links: raise fail(), naming the guide and the target, when a relative link points to a .md file under .tools/docs that is not a site guide (known pages and SKIP). Links to other file types (workflows, images, yaml) keep going to the GitHub blob. Add a failing-case test in tests/test_site.py (the existing test at line 36 covers only the pass case). That honours AGENTS.md 'No silent fallbacks'. Because it will stop the build on the current text, ship it in the same change as (b). (b) Template repo, .tools/docs/troubleshooting_installed_app.md:7: keep the page working for both readers by removing the link and the 'uninstalling guide' wording, for example 'after uninstalling the app from Settings > Apps > Installed apps'. Do not add an uninstall section to install.md unless someone has tested it on all three systems. Drop the external-link checker from this change. At most, run a weekly non-blocking script that prints dead links to build/problems.md. The sandbox's 403/429 results are unverified, and an allowlist of bot-blocking hosts is more upkeep than a catalogue this small needs. Drop the form-repo changes (line 685 and the filename test), because the premise is wrong.

verdicts.misleading_risk: High. Parts are real (no 'last checked' statement; install.md has no disk-space note), but the proposal rests on evidence that does not carry over. 'Written for template version 0.1.15' is the template's current version, not a test statement, so the footer would claim guides were verified against 0.1.15 when nobody checked that, and it changes on every release with no review. The '6-8 minutes' counter-evidence is a headless Linux run (6 min 02 s NucleiSky, 1 min 02 s CellTracksColab, 1 min 17 s napari), which does not contradict a range across apps and OSes and says nothing about Windows or macOS. The 'Tested on' claim is already partly met: the napari guide says 'Tested on Linux. Windows and macOS are untested', and all three plugin guides carry an 'Under heavy construction ... untested' warning (user-guide.md line 6). The 'Last checked' lines, a staleness warning at 6 months and the plugin CI checks would add manual upkeep that will lapse in a small team, and a stale date is worse than none.

verdicts.misleading_risk: The gap is real but the proposal is too heavy. A docs-check workflow plus per-repo test scaffolding plus a ui-labels.yaml registry plus a reusable site workflow is a platform for a small team, and the benchmark itself warns against that. A label registry would be a second place where the labels are written, which conflicts with 'nothing written twice'. A grep-based 'guide matches code' test would be brittle, since labels are bold prose such as 'Validate & Add Submission' with an icon and different casing. The claim that nothing in the site's PR flow catches template changes is correct but incomplete: publish.yml checks out the template default branch, runs unit tests and builds on PRs of the site repo only, and the daily 05:23 UTC cron opens an issue on failure, so a rename that breaks a link or a guide registration is caught within a day. What none of it catches is wrong prose, which is the A1 failure.
verdicts.refined_proposal: Two cheap steps. (1) CellMigrationLab/LabConstrictor: add .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md with 3 checkboxes: 'Changes a button label, form field, workflow or artifact name, installer name or file path? Update the .tools/docs page that names it', 'Bumped template_version if users must act', 'Screenshots still valid'. Add the same two-line prompt to the CONTRIBUTING.md line 'Update documentation as needed' (the only mention today). (2) The same one-question template in LabConstrictor_streamlit and the three plugin repos, pointing to the guide file (docs/user-guide.md). Defer the automatic build check. If one is wanted later, a single workflow in the template that triggers on PRs touching .tools/docs/** and calls the site's existing scripts against the PR checkout is enough. It needs no new site code, since build_site.py already takes --template-dir. Drop CODEOWNERS, ui-labels.yaml and per-repo label tests: the registry would duplicate the labels, and the A1 fixes remove the only drift observed so far.
